session: This round was opened by the SESSION as M0-a-06's HARDENING ROUND S11 (J237 (2): the M0 hardening phase's fix rounds, batched per owning item; J238: M0 is the bedrock — the default for an M0 row is FIX with an exact precaution and a pin; J567: the bar is an independent closing check's PASS on the evidence), on THE CONTRACTS ROUND's kernel rows (J800 (3); J803): RL13 (queue Q205; the inventory's L26) — a batch's refusal names the body it refused — and RL15 (queue Q135) — the kernel's dry run and its façade member — with the leg's declared shift. Each 'failing line' below is one such row — an open queue row routed to this item (docs/M0-FIX-QUEUE.md) or a row the item's latest closing check wrote into its notes file; its evidence names the SOURCE you MUST read whole before fixing; the fix shape and the pin are the session's reading, binding unless the source or the code shows it wrong — then say so in your notes and do what the finding needs. THE RULES OF A HARDENING ROUND: (1) inside the item's owns and nowhere else — a row that needs another item's file is REPORTED, not built; FOR THIS ROUND the seats write inside THE WRITE SCOPE: M0-a-06's owns (plat/packages/kernel/src/tx/ and plat/packages/kernel/test/tx/, unchanged in M0-work.json) plus THE CROSS-ITEM SCOPE (LEG 1's OWN TEXT below); wherever this brief or plat/docs/build/M0.md §3 says 'inside the item's owns', read 'inside the write scope'; a change any other file would need, or any other change in a scope file, is REPORTED, not built; (2) every row gets a PIN (a test that is red without the fix; your mutant table shows each pin killing its mutant) unless the row is comment-only or asks for a choices row — then the text is the deliverable; (3) BEHAVIOUR: a hardening fix may move output where a defect is fixed — a DECLARED shift, stated in your choices row with the before and after (digests and goldens re-recorded in the same round, named), never silent; where a row offers alternatives, take the one the design's text supports and say which; a change of an operation's or stage's CONTRACT (its design-level behaviour, a record or file format, an exported API) is NOT yours — report it as a note for the session's ruling and leave the row at REPORTED; (4) J264 / N-58: the refusal census of the item's registered families before and after the round, never rising (a row whose fix makes a lawful input succeed lowers it and says so); (5) API frozen (J263 Q1): no export of a folder index or the barrel added, removed or renamed unless a row explicitly asks for one — then the index change is the row's and stated; message texts pinned verbatim where a row changes one (J263 Q6); (6) the gates, NEAR and RELATED@1000 as the brief above says, at W=1; (7) the item's notes file gains a section 'Hardening round S11' with the row-by-row outcome (fixed / pinned / reported, each with its evidence and mutant), and the round's choices row names every row it closes. The CLOSING CHECKER confirms every row's outcome with its own evidence (re-reading the source note or queue row), re-kills every pin's mutant, re-measures the refusal census, and judges new findings by the blocker rule only; a row left REPORTED with a stated contract reason is not a failing line. THIS IS LEG 1 OF A MERGED ROUND OF THREE LEGS — THE CONTRACTS ROUND, M0-a-06's (the MERGED-ROUND RULE, J443; J803 R1, R2): M0-a-06 S11 → M0-e-03 S6 → M0-c-04 S8, in that order, on ONE tree and ONE branch, no reset between, each leg with its own build, closing check, LANDED line and record; EACH LEG LAUNCHES ONLY IF THE LEG BEFORE IT PASSED (ok with check.verdict pass) — legs 2 and 3 share no file, but @plat/layout depends on @plat/site, so a failed leg 2 must never sit under leg 3's gates: a failure HANDS BACK, and the session launches what is left. Legs 2 and 3 also wait on the landings of the rounds now in flight on their items (M0-e-03 S5, child EA; M0-c-04 S7, child EC). The round carries no leg of M0-a-05: the refusal that names a body is made by the transaction at commit (kernel/src/tx/tx.ts roleProblems → run → reject), and a plan that commits nothing for a SEQUENCE of splits is a dry run, which only tx/ can open and undo (docs/validation/a05-contracts-spec-2026-11-13/draft.md §0, §1.1, §1.3 (c)). lines.required_change: BUILD (J803 R7, R12, R13): tx/tx.ts exports `dryRun<T>(p: Plat, spec: KernelTx, fn: (overlay: Overlay) => KernelResult<T>, env: TxEnv = {}): KernelResult<T>` — the callback form only (`spec.ops` empty) and `spec.expect` empty, both asserted; `open(p, spec, env)` with every check of it; `fn` on the overlay; then, WHATEVER `fn` returned, the batch undone to its frame (`undoBatch`) and closed; `{ ok: false, code: 'E_WORK_LIMIT', detail: workDetail(t, 'the dry run exceeded its work limit') }` when `overWork`, else `fn`'s result as it returned it; no commit row, no record, no `onCommit`; a throw undone and rethrown as `tx` rethrows (`rethrown`, its form 'dry'). Its doc says it is 'undone exactly as a rejected batch is (§3.3's frames)' and names what that does NOT undo — the per-arena diagnostics outside the undo log: kerb's last read, bandUnion's closings, the neighbour maps, the level-digest states (R13). Read BY PATH by the façade; no index or barrel line (J263 Q1).
